_illustrative: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY: PR 9999 in acme/widgets on git.example.com is fictional. Copy the shape, never the facts.

pr.title: feat(reset): cap password-reset mails at 3 per minute
pr.author: dana

existing_comments.note: 1 bot thread asking to log the 429 — answered by the author; nothing below repeats it

what_it_does: Anyone could ask for unlimited password-reset mails to any address, so one inbox could be flooded.
This PR counts reset requests and refuses the 4th within 60 seconds with `429 Try again later`.
The count is kept in memory on each server.
summary.reason: The cap counts per sender IP, so an attacker with 2 IPs still sends 6 mails a minute to one inbox — the exact problem the PR is meant to stop.

items.title: Cap is per sender IP, not per email address
items.why: The issue is about flooding ONE inbox. Keyed on the IP, 2 IPs send 6 mails a minute to the same address.
items.comment: The cap is keyed on the sender IP, so `--ips 198.51.100.7,203.0.113.9` still sends 6 mails a minute to `user@acme.test`; issue 9990 asks for 3 per address. Could we key it on the email instead?

change.checked: applies cleanly — typecheck not run (no node_modules in the snapshot)

items.title: How many API instances run in production?
items.why: Each server counts alone. With 4 servers the real cap is about 12 a minute, not 3. Fine for one server, wrong for many.

also_ask.say: How many replicas does the `api` deployment run in production today (`kubectl get deploy api -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'`)? We need it for the reset-mail cap in PR 9999.

items.comment: This `Map` lives in one process. If prod runs more than 1 instance (the LB spreads calls), the effective cap is 3 × instances. How many run today, and is a shared counter (e.g. Redis `INCR` with a 60 s TTL) planned before we turn this on?

evidence.detail: `private readonly hits = new Map<string, number[]>()` — per process; replica count not visible in this repo

items.confirm_by: `kubectl get deploy api -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'` in prod; > 1 means the cap is multiplied
items.unknown: Whether prod runs more than one API instance

items.title: Test the 4th call is refused

items.comment: The spec only checks that the 1st call passes. Could we add a case where the 4th call within 60 s returns `false`?
